A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TELLME research. All 25 pages of v2 and 28 pages of v3, including figures, tables, equations, and appendices, support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original representation-disentanglement, monitoring, detoxification, and ablation results, including additional experiments in Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 reports original monitoring and detoxification results, multimodal and scaling evaluations, and additional analyses in the main text and Appendix A.

M1.justification: For monitoring, v2 Appendix B.3 specifies the last QA token, whereas v3 Section 4.1 averages losses at the last input and output tokens. v3 also introduces simultaneous training at three layer depths in Appendix A.5. The core contrastive/retain-loss framework is retained, and using both token positions without KL regularization for detoxification already appeared in v2.

E1.justification: v3 adds reward-hacking/misalignment detection and image-text safety training using SPA-VL and RLHF-V, with evaluation on MM-Safety, VLSBench, and MSSBench. MMMU and MMLU-Pro extend capability evaluation. CoLA, SiQA, and math/knowledge ablations are retained from v2 rather than newly introduced.

E2.justification: v2 Table 5 evaluates Self-Sim, Linear Probe, Latent Guard, and SFT monitors. v3 Table 1 removes Latent Guard, uses a prompted Judge, and adds SAE, SAE-KL, SAE-Multi-TopK, Transcoder, and Skip Transcoder comparisons. Appendix A.3 adds a pretrained Gemma SAE comparison, while retaining some post-SFT monitoring results.

E3.justification: Reported learning rate, lambda, and sigma change from 0.001, 0.1, and 0.1 in v2 Table 7 to 0.0002, 10, and 0.07 in v3 Table 6. New evaluations introduce larger dense/MoE configurations, distributed training, and benchmark-specific multimodal scoring procedures. These are reported setting changes and additions; the PDFs do not establish that all retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds single-versus-multiple-layer training comparisons, lambda/alpha sensitivity sweeps, an empirical k-variance check, and a behavior-versus-word-overlap case study. It also examines transfer from multimodal training to text safety. Existing contrastive-loss, retain-loss, and layer-depth analyses remain, while quantitative detoxification studies comparing SFT/TELLME ordering are removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed/run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The same 0.47% standard deviation across target-layer choices is retained. v3's added k-variance proxy measures representation dispersion rather than uncertainty across experimental runs.

E6.justification: v3 replaces monitoring results under revised settings and adds misalignment, multi-layer, and multimodal/scaling outcomes. Llama's safety Hausdorff entries change from 2.68/5.74 for Origin/TELLME in v2 Table 1 to 9.92/39.27 in v3 Table 4. Most retained detoxification scores match, but SFT-combination rows, math/knowledge disentanglement scores, and much of the earlier detailed capability matrix are removed.

T1.justification: The Wasserstein and k-variance definitions, classification-margin bound, proof, and Lipschitz/better-classifier assumptions are retained from v2 Section 2.2 and Appendix C in v3 Appendix B. Relocation, revised interpretation, and the added empirical proxy do not introduce new formal mathematics.

C1.justification: v3 makes robustness across modalities, dense/MoE architectures, and parameter scales a central contribution, extending v2's emphasis on disentanglement across math, knowledge, and safety. The abstract and conclusion also narrow the theoretical pitch from explaining LLM generalization to analyzing behavior-level monitoring through an existing generalization bound.

C2.justification: v3 newly acknowledges label-informed grouping and limitations of fair SAE comparisons, discusses judge errors, and offers an alignment-disruption explanation for SFT's safety degradation. It adds interpretations concerning cross-layer interference, multimodal transfer, and behavioral rather than lexical separation. The dedicated limitations paragraph remains substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds SAE expansion/top-k settings and parameter counts, judge identities, a misalignment prompt, and LLaMA-Factory/FSDP2 implementation details. The TELLME code link supplied in v2 disappears, without establishing that the code itself became unavailable. Documentation also becomes inconsistent: v3 Table 6 specifies sigma 0.07 while Appendix A.2 still states 0.1.

R1.justification: v3 substantially develops positioning against SAE/Transcoder approaches, discussing constraints of external decoding and TELLME's label-informed training advantage. It adds relevant transcoder, feature-consistency, and misalignment-monitoring literature, including Dunefsky et al., Paulo and colleagues, and Chan et al. Much earlier related work is retained; its relocation alone is not counted.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten, and the narrative is reorganized around monitoring, detoxification, scalability, ablations, and analysis. Related work moves into the main text, formal theory moves into the appendix, and the algorithm moves into the method section. SEER terminology is cleaned up, with additional authorship and front-matter changes.

P2.justification: The main text adopts a two-column conference layout, the monitoring table is redesigned, and new scaling plots and comparison tables are added. The t-SNE display is reduced to safety and split between the main text and appendix; algorithm and case-study displays are relocated. v3 Table 3 also corrects the swapped AGIEval/GSM8K headers in v2 Table 4.

improvement.justification: Direct SAE/Transcoder comparisons, additional ablations, explicit fairness qualifications, and narrower theoretical claims improve support for the central monitoring argument. The net gain is limited by removed code-access information and new reporting inconsistencies: conflicting temperature settings, disagreement between Figure 3 and Table 11's Qwen2.5 scaling trends, and a Hausdorff improvement summary in Appendix A.2 that does not match Table 4.
